title: Cell-5 Heading Before Related Columns

illustrates.quote: Maintaining the hierarchy of headings in a document is important, and there may be times when columned material will follow a cell-5 heading. Insert a blank line to separate the cell-5 heading from the columns so it is clear the heading is related to all columns.

blocks.features: Bold white-on-navy three-column table header bar.

Five plain three-column, comparative-forms-related data rows below the header bar; the braille joins each row with dot-5 guide dots (a related-columns table), which this section's heading/paragraph/list-item print-block schema has no dedicated block type for.

print.notes: Illustrates a blank line inserted between a cell-5 heading and the related three-column table that follows it, per rule 4.5.4. The table itself (header bar + 5 related-columns data rows, joined by guide dots) is recorded as `other` because it needs Emboss's table/related-columns formatting, which this gold-run harness's print.blocks model (heading/paragraph/list-item/other) does not build -- see standards-findings.md.
print.printFeatures: Left-aligned blue heading above a three-column table with a bold white-on-navy header bar (Positive/Comparative/Superlative) and five plain data rows.

braille.notes: Line 1 blank; line 2 the cell-5 heading 'Irregular Adverbs'; line 3 blank, per 4.5.4; line 4 the three column headers; line 5 three dot-5 guide-dot separator segments; lines 6-10 the five related-columns data rows; line 11 blank.

uncertain: The header bar and data rows are a related-columns table (BANA §8/§4.5.4), not a plain single-column list; this gold-run harness's print.blocks kinds (heading/paragraph/list-item/other) have no table block type, so this content is recorded as `other` (excluded from the model) rather than built inaccurately as a plain list. Expect gold-run.mjs to report a mismatch/not-representable status limited to the missing table rows, not the heading itself.
resolution: braille.lines agree. `kind` for the table rows resolved to `other` rather than run B's per-row `list-item`: this section's print.blocks-to-model mapping (task brief: heading/paragraph/list-item/other) has no representation for guide-dot-joined related columns, so tagging the rows `list-item` would build them as a plain unrelated single-column list and produce a *silently wrong* model rather than a documented limitation; `other` is the honest choice, matching gold-run.mjs's own "never invent, always record" precedent from §11.
